core_job: The spec turns the app into a real local-network remote for TV and lighting gear the user already owns. It drives Roku TVs and players through Roku's published External Control Protocol, ECP (port 8060, plain HTTP, no auth; checked 2026-10-12 in developer.roku.com's external-control-api doc). It drives WLED LED controllers through the WLED JSON API (/json/state, /json/info, /json/eff; checked in kno.wled.ge). It also calls webhooks for a hub the user runs, such as Home Assistant's POST /api/webhook/<id> (checked in home-assistant.io). The flow: scan the phone's /24 subnet to find devices, add them by room, use a Roku remote that shows only the keys that model reports it supports and can type through the phone keyboard (Lit_ keys), and use a WLED panel that first reads the device's real state. Today's app controls nothing real. It runs a 'Simulator mode' by default (app_en.arb:24). Its only real transport posts to an invented /remote/command contract that no product implements (http_hub_transport.dart:22-24 says so itself). The PlayStation-style game pad's 'Pair' button only flips a flag. Netflix/YouTube/Disney+ tiles and a light wattage 'estimate' are pretend.
signature: Scenes across brands. An ordered, timed list of steps across Roku (key presses, launching a channel by its ID), WLED (power, brightness, colour, effect, preset, nightlight fade) and webhooks, run with one tap from the Home screen, phone straight to device, with no server or account. Every run produces a report from the real HTTP results (status code and ms for each step), saved to history and copyable. Among the App Store descriptions checked with the iTunes Search API on 2026-10-12, single-brand apps control one brand: Roku Remote Official (6.27M ratings), Rokie, five WLED apps, Philips Hue. Home Assistant does cross-brand scenes, but only with a server the user installs and maintains. Competitor behaviour beyond those descriptions is not verified; WebSearch was unavailable.
must: M1 Remove the fiction: simulator mode as a user-facing mode, the invented /remote/command + /health hub contract (an existing hub URL migrates to a Webhook device), the PlayStation-style game pad tab, the streaming-brand tiles, the keys ECP does not support (number pad, Guide, Subtitles, Voice, Source), the free-floating light zones and kLightScenes, and the wattage estimate. Old devices/rooms data is migrated with a one-time note, so nothing is lost silently. Grep for banned strings returns 0 hits.

M2 Find and add real devices: an explainer, then a /24 unicast scan (GET :8060/query/device-info and :80/json/info, 600 ms timeout, at most 24 requests in flight, cancellable). Honest not-on-Wi-Fi and nothing-found states, including the Roku 'Control by mobile apps' hint. Add-by-IP must answer the probe before saving. Webhooks follow the LAN-or-https rule. Add NSAllowsLocalNetworking, an explicit Android INTERNET permission and a cleartext config, and verify on the emulator.

M3 Real Roku remote and WLED panel behind the existing DeviceTransport seam. Keys are gated on what device-info reports. Power off only, because power-on is not in the documented key list. Type sheet sends Lit_ keys. Real power-mode readout. Volume/channel numbers are removed because ECP does not report them. WLED state is read before any control shows, effects come from the device, presets 1-250, nightlight timer, power shown only from info.leds.pwr. Rollback on failure is kept. MockClient tests assert the exact requests.

M4 Signature: Scenes across brands, with editor, per-step test, sequential run with live progress and cancel, persisted history capped at 100, Copy report. No ads or interstitial in the scene flow. A widget test runs a 3-step mixed scene with one 500 failure and checks that the run persists.

M5 Depth: rooms with real last-answered status dots, a History screen with device/scene/failures-only filters and search, Copy/Paste setup as JSON with merge rules and malformed-input handling (no share_plus, because of the Podfile.lock trap), and Forget everything.

M6 Own identity: no bottom tab bar; Home = Scenes keycap grid + rooms. Remote styled as a physical handset with a signal LED that shows the real HTTP outcome. 'Bone & signal' palette (light primary #A8431A on #ECE8DF/#FAF8F4, dark primary #F28C55 on #141311; contrast all >= 4.5, computed), ThemeMode.system. Saira (variable) + Space Mono, bundled, curl-verified, unused elsewhere in the portfolio. 10 px keycap / 6 px card shape. Own 3-page onboarding. Cupertino on iOS. Hand-built icon, not generate_app_icons.py:75. New splash (shasum not 3f6a9b27...). Exactly one AglAdBanner. onTransition only when leaving the scene editor. All names come from one kAppName.

M7 Settings and copy for this app (Devices, Scan, History, Setup, Feel, rewritten 'What leaves this phone', Privacy choices kept, How it works, Forget everything, About). All new strings translated in all 12 ARB files, because l10n_test enforces it.

M8 Proven: flutter analyze clean; tests pass against the 367 baseline; tests removed with deleted code are named in the commit; identity and source-grep tests; iOS simulator screenshots of every new screen. A dev-only LAN harness (doc-sample responses, never used for store shots) proves the exact requests; an Android emulator cleartext check. Path-limited commit, never fastlane/ or the dirty Podfile.lock. Real-hardware runs are a human step, not verified.
